description: bash init.sh installs what's missing, installs git hooks, validates content, starts the Vite dev server and waits for a real 200 serving the app shell.

Executable layer rules: domain/application/content/infrastructure/game/features boundaries; Phaser only in src/game; IndexedDB only in persistence; React only in UI; Phaser and chapters lazy; no network, eval, any or console.log.

The PreToolUse guard blocks only unrecoverable commands (force-push, history rewrites, hook bypass, recursive deletes of home or root, cloud deploys, npm publish) and allows everything else, including merges, pushes to main and workflow runs — verified by its two-directional self-test (never an inline probe).
Strict TypeScript (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, no implicit any) type-checks cleanly.
ESLint (typescript-eslint strict, react-hooks, jsx-a11y strict) with zero warnings, and Prettier formatting.
verification: npm run --silent lint && npm run --silent format:check

description: Road to Jericho content passes Zod schemas, referential integrity, reachability from every spawn, and governance rules (no embedded verse text, cited history, labelled paraphrase).
verification: npm run --silent content:validate && npx --no-install vitest run --project unit tests/content

description: Content predicates and effects are declarative data evaluated by pure, tested functions (no executable code in content).
verification: npx --no-install vitest run --project unit tests/unit/domain/conditions.test.ts tests/unit/domain/effects.test.ts tests/unit/domain/inventory.test.ts

description: Deterministic quest engine: stages, objectives, optional objectives, prerequisites, outcomes with rewards, alternate/fail outcomes, journal hooks.
Branching dialogue: conditional entries, hidden and visibly-unavailable choices with reasons, once-only choices, conditional branches, history, graceful missing-node handling.
Packing (resource allocation), measuring (environmental logic), deduction (evidence-backed route choice) and sequence (ordering evidence + an explicitly uncertain conclusion), with tiered hints.
Versioned saves with step-by-step migrations, tested against v1 fixtures, corrupt data, tampered data and future versions.
Content records carry kind, sources, confidence, sensitivity, review status and version history; AI drafts cannot skip steps to approval; approval needs a named human.
Headless playthroughs of every major branch (caravan help, walk + night + dawn delivery, send help, hurry past) complete the chapter through the real application layer.
IndexedDB repositories for profiles, saves (indexed per profile) and settings; memory fallback; autosave debouncing; profile deletion removes its saves.
No Bible text displays unless a public-domain/licensed translation is approved; the exact placeholder shows otherwise. WEB Luke 10:25-37 is stored but disabled.
React UI tests (menus, profiles, settings incl. key remapping, journal tabs, quest log, dialogue, puzzles, Scripture Connection, summary) with axe-core checks.
knip finds no unused files, exports or dependencies (domain-model types are marked @public).
Production build with PWA manifest and service worker; Phaser and chapter content split into lazy chunks.
verification: npx --no-install vite build >/dev/null && test -f dist/sw.js && test -f dist/manifest.webmanifest && ls dist/assets | grep -q '^mount-world' && ls dist/assets | grep -q '^road-to-jericho'

description: Builds for a repository sub-path (GitHub Pages): assets, icons, manifest scope and service-worker fallback all use the base path.
verification: VITE_BASE_PATH=/witness/ npx --no-install vite build --outDir dist-subpath --emptyOutDir >/dev/null && grep -q '/witness/assets/' dist-subpath/index.html && grep -q '"scope":"/witness/"' dist-subpath/manifest.webmanifest && grep -q '/witness/index.html' dist-subpath/sw.js; rc=$?; rm -rf dist-subpath; exit $rc

description: Browser E2E: create profile, start chapter, conversation, quest, item, puzzle, choice + consequence, save, reload, restore, continue, complete, summary, Scripture references.
Smoke on desktop, phone and tablet viewports; manifest; keyboard-only play; touch controls; legacy v1 save restore + corrupt-save handling via the UI.
verification: npx --no-install playwright test e2e/smoke.spec.ts e2e/mobile.spec.ts e2e/saves.spec.ts

description: axe-core WCAG 2.2 AA scans in a real browser (incl. colour contrast and high-contrast mode) of title, settings, chapter select, dialogue, HUD, journal and quests.
After one visit, the installed app relaunches with no network and starts a chapter (Phaser + content from the precache).

Frame rate is measured while walking in the market (floor 20 fps under headless software rendering; 38 fps measured), and a CPU-throttled run checks that automatic simpler effects switch on. On-device 60 fps confirmation is a separate entry.

Exactly one world canvas; keyboard walking changes the picture and changing place redraws the world — on the production build AND the dev server (React StrictMode once left a frozen duplicate canvas).

Art direction per place (palette, materials, light, height, shadows, density), painted-site rules, people (noticing, blinking, talking, poses), camera framing and look-ahead, crowds, time-of-day light and the automatic-quality decision.

Each place sounds different (market voices and clinks, hearth crackle, gusts, birdsong and water), moments have distinct sounds (a bell for clues), music plays modal phrases; the synth runs against a fake WebAudio context and captions what is audible.
A gamepad can play the whole chapter: d-pad/stick moves focus in menus, dialogue and puzzles, A presses, B goes back, LB opens Go to (simulated pad).
The opening plays under the strict Content-Security-Policy recommended in docs/security-privacy.md with no violation reports (Zod runs jitless).
Domain events are built only where EVENT_OWNERS says; memory and IndexedDB repositories pass one shared contract.
Run the smoke and full-chapter E2E on WebKit (the iOS/iPadOS Safari engine). Needs a webkit project in playwright.config.ts and: npx playwright install webkit.
HUMAN: a named editor proofreads the stored WEB text of Luke 10:25-37 against ebible.org and sets approvedForDisplay: true (recording their name in the commit and the approval log).
verification: npx --no-install tsx -e "import { TRANSLATIONS } from './src/content/scripture/translations.ts'; process.exit(TRANSLATIONS.some((t) => t.approvedForDisplay) ? 0 : 1)"

description: Merging to main publishes the site: the Pages workflow deploys the exact commit once CI succeeds on a push to main in this repository (never a failed run, another branch or a fork), built for the repository sub-path.

Chapter 3, A Journey to Bethlehem (Luke 2:1-20), is playable end to end as content only: the player is a fictional child of a crowded Bethlehem household during the registration; four puzzle types (measuring, packing, optional sequence side quest, deduction); choices that show in the world (what stays in the guest room, the lost lamb, where the stranger Zerah sleeps, what to do with the shepherds' news); the people of Luke 2 stay off-stage and are heard of only through Scripture references and a neighbor's labelled paraphrase; every educational record cites retrieved sources and awaits human review.

Chapter 4, A Letter from Paul (Philemon and Colossians 4:7-18): four scenes in Colossae and the Lycus valley, all four puzzle types, an optional side quest, story-driven rain, choices visible in the world, silent biblical figures, open disputed questions, and headless playthroughs of every major branch to the summary.

Chapter 2, A Storm on Galilee (Mark 4:35–41): the player's fishing family is one of the "other boats". Playable from chapter select to the summary on every major branch, with four puzzle types, an optional side quest, choices that show in the world, and weather driven by the story; content integrity, reachability and governance verified.

A teaser film plays before a profile's first new game of Chapter 1 (and again from chapter select): a silent 3D film with the words as real text cued to its time, a synthesised score cued to it, Skip always available (button, Escape, Enter, Space), pause and play; under reduced motion or when the film can't load, the poster with the words stepped by Next; never replayed on its own once watched or skipped (profile.seenTeasers); the film is never cached by the service worker.
verification: npx --no-install vitest run tests/unit/domain/teaser.test.ts tests/content/teaser.test.ts tests/ui/teaser.test.tsx tests/unit/infrastructure/film-score.test.ts tests/unit/app/art-cache.test.ts

description: Each later chapter has two puzzle types of its own instead of packing and jar filling: Chapter 2 trim (load the boat level) and netting (mend a net by its row and column numbers); Chapter 3 logicGrid (places for supper) and floorplan (fit shaped pieces on the guest room floor); Chapter 4 map (follow written directions on a sketch) and dyeing (reach a named shade in limited dips). Each is a Zod schema plus pure checker, integrity-checked for one fair answer, keyboard-playable with every move announced, and keeps the old puzzle's id, place and effects.

Chapters 1 and 2 play 20–30 minutes for a first-time player. Chapter 1 adds Rivka's linen (packed with the remedy; a strip can bind Menashe), Eli the shepherd boy on the ridge (bread, what he saw, Shimon's message), Whose Cloak? (a deduction at the inn) and sitting with Natan before Yair's story. Chapter 2 adds Grandmother's corner (a first net), Hodaya of the Magdala crew, Oded's Leaking Boat (a sequence puzzle whose result shows in the storm), the lamp at the stern, seeing to the others, the net on the way home and telling Nikanor. Play time is measured headlessly; content added after the owner's approval stays awaiting review.
verification: npx --no-install vitest run tests/integration/play-time.test.ts tests/integration/playthrough.test.ts tests/integration/storm-on-galilee-playthrough.test.ts tests/content/road-to-jericho.test.ts tests/content/storm-on-galilee.test.ts tests/unit/content/approvals.test.ts

description: Every registered chapter has a design document, docs/chapters/<id>.md, in one fourteen-section template (docs/chapters/README.md) that names each of its scenes and each puzzle with its type; the README lists every chapter, and docs/chapter-authoring-guide.md takes a newcomer through adding one end to end.

Background music is four recorded Pixabay tracks (owner's decision 2026-10-01, ADR-0018) chosen by mood through AudioPort: oud and qanun for home, markets and menus; Sacred Sands for journeys; the mystery for danger and the storm; the flute for reflection, Scripture, Paul's letter and the endings. Cross-fades, no needless restarts, last request wins, loops, ducking under dialogue and reading, silence before Galilee's calm, tension that stops with the story, teaser music cued to the film; starts on a gesture, silent on failure, paused when muted or hidden, offline from its own range-request cache; credits in About this game; provenance checked by SHA-256.
